title: CAMPER: Exploring the Potential of Content Addressable Memory for 3D Point Cloud Efficient Range Search
problem: Real-time range search in large 3D point clouds generated by LiDAR is computationally expensive for autonomous driving applications. Existing systems struggle with the latency and power requirements of processing high-precision point clouds.
motivation: Autonomous driving systems require real-time processing of high-precision LiDAR point clouds, and range search is a critical bottleneck in this pipeline.
method: CAMPER is a CAM-centered accelerator that develops a ripple comparison 13T (RC-13T) CAM cell to perform distance comparisons natively in memory. It employs a spatial approximation search algorithm based on Chebyshev distance to reduce computational complexity while maintaining accuracy. The architecture supports flexibility and scalability for handling large point cloud datasets efficiently.
key_novelty: First exploration of Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) for efficient 3D point cloud range search, leveraging CAM's native in-memory comparison capabilities.
contributions: RC-13T CAM cell design for efficient distance comparison operations
Spatial approximation search algorithm based on Chebyshev distance for point cloud range queries
CAMPER accelerator achieving 10.4× throughput improvement over GPU and 228× energy efficiency gain over SOTA accelerators
Demonstration of CAM's viability and scalability for real-time point cloud processing
limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: CAM-based acceleration for point cloud range search
